conviction_note: Net +3.0: a $20.0m net IEEPA tariff recovery that DBI's own Q1 10-Q says it expects to recognise, held off the balance sheet as a gain contingency, whose realisation window (CBP CAPE payouts) is now confirmed by Caleres booking $55.6m in a quarter ending one day after DBI's, partly offset by Famous Footwear's -5.9% comp in the identical weeks against DBI's own flat-to-slightly-positive Q2 retail guide.

findings.finding: DBI's Q1 10-Q discloses it sold the rights to its IEEPA tariff claims to an unnamed Investor before the 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling and expects to recognise approximately $20.0m to income (claims value less the Investor's portion, net of proceeds already received) for tariff recoveries, with no receivable booked as of 2 May 2026 because it applied the gain-contingency model — $20.0m is ~$0.36/share pre-tax on 55.9m diluted shares and ~7% of the $290m market cap, and none of it is in the FY26 $0.28-$0.38 EPS guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Gain-contingency accounting means the number appears nowhere in the Q1 press release, nowhere in the reaffirmed FY guide, and nowhere in Q1 reported or adjusted EPS — it exists only in the Commitments & Contingencies note of a 10-Q for a company with two remaining sell-side analysts (UBS Neutral, Telsey Market Perform). If it were priced, the stock would not be -16.75% over twenty sessions into a print that can mechanically deliver ~7% of market cap in cash, and previews would frame the quarter around a tariff recovery instead of quoting a garbled adjusted-EPS consensus that aggregators variously print as $0.25, $0.22 and -$0.06. The claim-sale-to-an-Investor structure is also unique to DBI among footwear names and is not something a screen surfaces.
findings.independence: Caleres, a footwear importer whose Q2 ended 2 Aug 2026 (one day after DBI's 1 Aug quarter end), reported on 2026-09-09 that it recognised $55.6m of IEEPA tariff recoveries in cost of goods sold, which establishes that CBP CAPE payouts to footwear importers actually landed inside this exact fiscal window rather than slipping to Q3: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAL/caleres-reports-second-quarter-2026-cbjhhvcqm4mz.html . Home Depot's CBP lump sum arrived 'near the end of June', inside the same window: https://fortune.com/2026/08/19/home-depot-730-million-tariff-refund-largely-offset-rising-costs-cfo/

findings.finding: DBI's FY26 guidance conservatism rests on an assumption management stated on 9 Jun 2026 — that 'a substantial portion of any potential refunds will be offset by increased risk from the new Section 301 tariffs that may begin in August' — but the August step-up replaced an expiring Section 122 10% surcharge (lapsed 24 Jul 2026) with a two-tier 10%/12.5% Section 301 forced-labour duty, an incremental 0-2.5pp rather than a new layer, and Caleres guided H2 gross margin up 150-200bp citing 'lower current tariff rates'.
findings.why_not_priced: DBI's guide was set on 9 June against a tariff regime that had not yet been specified; the Section 122 expiry (24 Jul) and the shape of its Section 301 replacement were only settled in late July, after the last time DBI spoke publicly, so no DBI-sourced number reflects them. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading 30-45% below both surviving analyst targets while the only H2 downgrade in the file (UBS to $6 from $7.50 on 1 Sep 2026) is a valuation cut rather than a tariff-cost cut.
findings.independence: Shares the Caleres 2026-09-09 release with finding 1 as corroboration and should be collapsed into that source cluster to that extent; the primary evidence here is separate (the USTR Section 301 forced-labour action and the Section 122 expiry) and is corroborated independently at https://specialtyfabricsreview.com/2026/08/14/tariffs-14/ . The DBI June quote is from https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-designer-brands-q1-2026-shows-surprising-eps-beat-93CH-4733092

findings.finding: Caleres reported on 2026-09-09 that Famous Footwear — the closest listed analogue to DSW, off-mall US family footwear — had Q2 comps -5.9% and sales -6.3% with gross margin down 100bp, blamed on 'a later Back-to-School season and softness in lifestyle athletic', covering the identical May-1 August weeks in which DBI guided its Retail segment to comps 'flat to slightly positive'.
findings.why_not_priced: The Famous number is a segment line inside a release whose headline was a beat and a raise — consolidated sales +5.6%, Brand Portfolio +23.6%, adjusted EPS $0.47 versus ~$0.38 expected — and Caleres shares rose on it, so a reader taking the headline concludes footwear is fine. I am discounting this finding heavily rather than sizing it full, precisely because it had one full session to transmit into DBI before tomorrow's print, which is the opposite of the tariff finding. The size is also cut because DSW skews adult fashion where Famous skews kids/lifestyle-athletic, and Caleres itself said fashion 'continues to meaningfully outperform lifestyle athletic', so the same document argues DSW's mix is the relatively protected one; DBI also laps an easy -5.0% comp from Q2 2025.
findings.independence: DICK'S reported on 2026-08-25 that its Foot Locker segment ran proforma comps -3.6% on a 'challenging athletic footwear marketplace' with heavy dependence on legacy silhouettes, an independent same-quarter read on the athletic side: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/DKS/dick-s-sporting-goods-inc-reports-second-quarter-xca0mkeet3n1.html . Note this finding and finding 1 both cite the same Caleres document for different facts and should be collapsed to the larger residual on that cluster.

findings.finding: The sealed baseline's history block is wrong for a mechanical reason: EDGAR carries 'Designer Brands Inc.' as a former name with an end date of 2026-08-04 even though the name did not change, so the code discarded all 31 genuine prior DBI prints as belonging to a predecessor entity and fell back to a 3.14% deadband derived from 20-day realised vol.
findings.why_not_priced: Not a market claim — a defect in my own anchor, filed at zero impact so it does not touch the ranking. It matters only for how the signed number should be read: with no option chain, no skew and a nulled reaction history, the baseline states no priced direction at all, and the 3.14% deadband materially understates what DBI actually does on prints (the 9 Jun 2026 Q1 reaction alone was roughly -6% to -9%).
findings.independence: Confirmed by the company's own filing history under the same CIK and by the 9 Jun 2026 reaction reported at https://www.rttnews.com/3658965/designer-brands-sees-fy26-at-high-end-of-prior-guidance-range-posts-profit-in-q1-stock-down-5-6.aspx

searched_and_found_nothing: Coverage-drop hypothesis: false. UBS (Mauricio Serna) and Telsey both still cover and both acted in 2026; UBS cut its target to $6.00 from $7.50 on 2026-09-01. The 'one estimate' in the sweep row is an aggregator artifact, not dropped coverage — but consensus data on DBI is genuinely inconsistent across vendors ($0.25, $0.22 and -$0.06 for the same quarter), so any beat/miss framing on this name is unreliable.

Quiet 8-K: none. DBI has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-18, and the two that exist post-Q1 are routine — a $0.05 quarterly dividend (2026-06-10) and annual-meeting vote results plus Code of Regulations housekeeping (2026-06-18).
Form 4 cluster: the 17 filings on 2026-07-10 and two on 2026-08-04 are consistent with post-annual-meeting equity grant timing, not an insider signal.

Nike allocation: could not source a dated 2026 disclosure of DSW's current Nike assortment size or a Nike wholesale-rebuild comment made after DBI last spoke on 2026-06-09. Search results claiming a Nike-into-DSW launch 'kicking off in October 2026' trace to a WWD article whose ID (1238817378) places it well before the September 2026 Caleres piece (1239202991); I dropped the lead rather than date it wrongly.

Brand-portfolio impairment: no evidence of a fresh Camuto/Keds/Topo write-down being set up; Q1 Brand Portfolio grew ~19% and Caleres' Brand Portfolio +8.2% organic reads the wholesale fashion channel as healthy.

Covenant risk: not a live issue this quarter. ABL borrowings $360.7m against a $492.3m borrowing base, $138.5m availability, and the 1:1 fixed-charge covenant only springs below $47.3m of availability — roughly $91m of headroom.
Consumer-side signals: no usable dated DSW app-store review trend, loyalty-programme change, status-page or hiring-page evidence. The February 2026 layoffs are old and already reflected in Q1's SG&A.
Whether DBI will exclude the $20.0m from adjusted EPS as Caleres excluded its $57.4m: unresolved, and it is the main reason finding 1 carries an 8-point band rather than a point estimate.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up: the largest thing I found is a positive, mechanically-quantified $20.0m cash item sitting in a footnote of a name that is -16.75% over twenty sessions, and with no option chain there is no skew to agree or disagree with — but the honest caveat is that the one negative I found (Famous Footwear -5.9%) is also the one that has already had a full session to reach the tape.
